verdict.rationale: Figma's own documentation shows that it publishes resources across teams, centralizes libraries, and offers library analytics that count component instances across all files. This confirms that shared component libraries reach beyond a single file. However, nothing in the evidence describes styles being published through libraries, or any controlled review-and-accept flow for updates when the source library changes. missing for 10: documented controlled update/accept-changes flow for library consumers, explicit evidence of styles published via libraries, in-depth library publishing docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, shared libraries publish components and styles across files and projects, with controlled updates when the source changes

citations.quote: Want to centralize assets, libraries, and workflows across departments
Get summary information about how many instances of a library's components exist across all files.
Get time series data about what actions your users have performed with your library's components on a week-by-week basis.
